boundary: Pillow unreadable-source OSError/ValueError behavior is preserved; readable non-JPEG or unsafe canonical bytes are dirty.
Single complete JPEG with SOI at start and true EOI at exact EOF; length-delimited payloads, all entropy scans, FF00 stuffing and restart markers are walked.
Only exact first, single, 14-byte JFIF1.01/units0/densities1x1/no-thumbnail APP0 is allowed; APP1-15/COM/unsupported extension payloads are refused anywhere.
Supported frame syntax is Huffman DCT C0/C1/C2; DNL, DAC, lossless/arithmetic modes and delayed dimensions are refused.

DQT8/16-bit entries and DHT counts/symbols fully consume the segment; unknown types/destinations, zero quantization values, incomplete/padded entries, empty or oversubscribed/all-ones Huffman trees are refused. DRI is exactly two bytes.
Each definition generation must be consumed by actual scan component/table use, not SOF or inactive selector fields. Replacing an unconsumed definition and any unused definition at EOI are refused.

Progressive initial DC consumes DC Huffman; DC refinement consumes none; AC consumes AC Huffman. Unused selectors must be zero. Quantization changes after first scan are refused as a conservative canonical-profile bound.
Valid progressive consumed Huffman updates, multiple entries, actual stuffing/restarts, 8/16-bit consumed quantization and optional absent APP0 remain supported.

Each sequential component appears in one scan. Progressive initializations happen once per coefficient band, AC follows initial DC, and refinement must match the prior coefficient bit plane; valid coarse/partial progressive interchange need not reach Al0 or code every AC band.

Pending definition consumption is committed only at the end of a scan with actual entropy bytes; an empty SOS header cannot launder a table. Duplicate/impossible scan history is refused even with arbitrary nonempty ignored bytes.
Sanitizer output is byte-for-byte identical to the prior re-encoding output; input private metadata sanitization still accepts supported source formats.
